# Language and writing-system specimen {#sec-language-and-script}

This appendix exercises language metadata separately from translated content.
The primary edition is tagged `en-US`; local spans identify their own language
so shaping, hyphenation, direction, and assistive technology do not inherit an
incorrect English assumption.

## Language-tagged prose {#sec-language-tagged-prose}

[English: The characteristically interdisciplinary electromechanical laboratory
documents reusable publishing experiments.]{.language-sample lang="en-US"}

<!-- writing-override: Locked French and German dictionaries are not installed for these localization specimens. -->
<!-- cspell:disable -->
[Français&#8239;: L’internationalisation électromagnétique demande une typographie
cohérente et une césure adaptée à la langue.]{.language-sample lang="fr-FR"}

[Deutsch: Die Donaudampfschifffahrtsgesellschaft dokumentiert wiederverwendbare
Veröffentlichungsexperimente.]{.language-sample lang="de-DE"}
<!-- cspell:enable -->

The language tags, rather than manual discretionary hyphens, select available
hyphenation behavior. An edition must load and validate the patterns required
by its primary and embedded languages before publication.

## Mixed writing systems {#sec-mixed-writing-systems}

<!-- writing-override: Locked Greek, Russian, and Hebrew dictionaries are not installed for these script specimens. -->
<!-- cspell:disable -->
- Greek: [Η τεχνολογία εξελίσσεται μέσα από τη γνώση.]{lang="el-GR"}
- Cyrillic: [Технология развивается благодаря знаниям.]{lang="ru-RU"}
- Hebrew: [הטכנולוגיה מתפתחת באמצעות ידע.]{lang="he-IL" dir="rtl"}
<!-- cspell:enable -->

These scripts are present in the selected Libertinus faces. Arabic, CJK,
Indic, and other scripts are not claimed by this baseline: a book using one
must add a locked, licensed family and locale profile before the glyph-coverage
check can pass.

## Nonbreaking conventions {#sec-nonbreaking-conventions}

Use a visible HTML entity in Markdown when a line break would change or obscure
meaning: `25&nbsp;MHz` produces 25&nbsp;MHz, and
`Figure&nbsp;1` produces Figure&nbsp;1. French punctuation may use an
explicit narrow no-break space, as in `français&#8239;:` above. Do not
insert invisible spacing characters casually; reserve them for a documented
language or technical convention.

Breaking spaces remain ordinary everywhere else. Nonbreaking spaces do not
replace semantic units, cross-references, or locale-aware number formatting.
